title: Streaming engine: operations handed to the in-memory engine
verdict: per-node fallback for opaque UDFs, some joins, some group-bys, keep-last unique, median and implode, cumulative eval and non-elementwise functions
description: The streaming engine lowers the optimized plan node by node (`lower_ir`, `lower_expr`, `lower_group_by` in crates/polars-stream). What it cannot stream it wraps in a fallback node that sinks its whole input into a `DataFrame` and runs the in-memory engine on it: `InMemoryMap`, `InMemoryJoin` and `ColumnarFunction`, which the plan visualizer colours as "in-memory engine fallback". The rest of the query keeps streaming; there is no whole-query fallback (polars-exec-engine).

Relations that fall back: a `MapFunction` that is not streamable (`rechunk`, a fast count, an opaque Python or Rust UDF not marked streamable, such as `LazyFrame.map_batches`); a join that is not an equi, semi, anti, cross or range join, an as-of join whose `by` keys are not known sorted the same way, a join with a non-equality condition other than a fused predicate, and any join with `validate`; `unique(keep="last", maintain_order=True)`; a group-by with an `apply`, with rolling or dynamic options (when not handled by the sorted rolling node), over object columns, or whose aggregations the streaming group-by cannot split (more than one non-elementwise input to one aggregation, non-elementwise post-processing, all expressions input-independent); an anonymous scan.

Expressions that fall back, each computed over the full input in its own node: `median` and `implode` as plain aggregations, a cumulative `eval`, a window `over` that cannot be lowered to a streaming group-by, and every non-elementwise function or UDF without its own streaming rule (`ColumnarFunction`), such as `map_batches` without `is_elementwise=True`.

What changes in a fallback node: the in-memory engine's algorithms (float sums, `group_by` row order) apply to that node's materialized input, so a fact probed in memory holds there, and one probed streaming may not. Evaluation order is the same in both: both evaluate expressions with polars-expr's physical expressions, so the masking of elementwise `when/then` branches (polars-exec-when-eager) applies in a fallback node too; a non-elementwise branch is computed over every row in either engine.

sverify's Polars translation reaches several of these: `map_batches` without `is_elementwise` (`_on_days`, the measure results), `search_sorted` over a whole column (a RANGE frame's bounds without PARTITION BY; per partition, under `over`, it streams), `implode` in an ungrouped aggregation, and `over`. Probes of `explain(engine="streaming")` for each translated construct go to the next round.
The docs are silent on which constructs fall back and a fallback node's results differing: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the fallback of `map_batches`, `LazyFrame.map_batches` or `implode`; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference has no engines. A profile's facts hold for the engine they were probed on; sverify pins the streaming engine (#605), so a fact whose construct falls back must hold for the in-memory engine as well, and a probe must check which engine ran it.

notes: `show_graph(engine='streaming', plan_stage='physical')` on Polars 2.1.0, macOS arm64: `cum_sum`, `cum_min`, `cum_max`, `forward_fill`, `shift`, `gather` with an index column, and `min`, `max`, `cum_sum`, `search_sorted` under `over(...)` stream; `cum_sum(reverse=True)` is a `columnar-function` fallback, and under `over` an `in-memory-map`; `search_sorted` without `over` is a `columnar-function` fallback; `join_asof` with `by` is an `in-memory-join`.

Polars divides by a column broadcast from a scalar (`g.max()` in `with_columns`) through its reciprocal, as by a literal (polars-double-scalar-divisor): 10 / 11 gave 0.9090909090909092, and 0.9090909090909091 once the divisor is a computed column.
